rounds.text: Precot Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 11.4x and an EV/EBITDA of 7.06x, both sitting below their respective sector benchmarks of 14.55x and 9x [E1, E6, E11]. Profitability metrics strongly outpace sector baselines, with a return on equity of 13.98% versus the sector benchmark of 7.19%, and a ROCE of 15.31% against a sector benchmark of 8.39% [E9, E10]. Operational momentum is powerful, highlighted by TTM sales growth of 16% and TTM profit growth of 65%, alongside an expanding operating margin reaching 19% in September 2026 compared to 12% a year prior [E17, E21, E31]. Cash generation is robust, backed by a Mar 2026 cash conversion ratio of 2.50x, delivering Rs 90 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 25 Cr in free cash flow [E34, E35, E36]. The broader textile sector provides a supportive macro backdrop, currently reading as a tailwind with a score of +0.57, validating the company's rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 [E61, E70]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over a 3-year period sits at -2%, and the yearly operating-margin trend reads inconsistent over the last two years [E16, E32].

Despite recent short-term earnings acceleration, Precot Ltd suffers from chronically weak core top-line expansion, evidenced by a sluggish 3% compounded sales growth rate over the last decade and a contraction of -2% over the past three years [E14, E16]. This secular stagnation is mirrored in poor multi-year profitability returns, highlighted by a low 10-year median return on equity of 2% and a low recent ROE of 7.7% [E13, E26]. Furthermore, the company carries heavy debt obligations with borrowings sitting at Rs 350 Cr, accompanied by a thin current ratio buffer of 1.14x and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E32, E38, E39]. The stock also bears extreme historical risk, suffering a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -91.3% alongside an annualized volatility of 53.6% [E53, E54]. Conceded: [E21], the company has experienced strong recent profit growth over the trailing twelve months.

Conceded: [E14, E16] regarding the multi-year and 3-year historical sales figures. However, that secular stagnation argument ignores the explosive operational inflection happening right now, evidenced by a 16% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 32% YoY sales surge [E17, E62]. This top-line momentum is translating into massive earnings power, with 3-year profit growth at 48% and TTM profit growth reaching 65% [E20, E21]. The bear's critique of historical returns overlooks that Precot's current efficiency metrics decisively outpace sector benchmarks, with an ROCE of 15.31% versus the sector's 8.39% and an ROE of 13.98% against a sector 7.19% [E9, E10]. Operating margins have also expanded by 7 percentage points to 16% in the TTM and 19% in the September 2026 quarter, proving the business is structurally improving rather than stagnating [E30, E31]. Conceded: [E32, E38, E53, E54] concerning inconsistent margin trends, thin current ratio buffers, and severe historical drawdowns and volatility. Yet these risks are heavily mitigated by stellar cash generation, featuring Rs 90 Cr in operating cash flow and a 2.50x cash conversion rate that fully backs reported profits, all supported by a favorable textile sector tailwind [E34, E35, E70].

The bull relies heavily on recent short-term acceleration [E17, E62], but that obscures a multi-year structural pattern of dismal top-line stagnation, highlighted by a meager 3% compounded sales growth over 10 years and a contraction of -2% over 3 years [E14, E16]. While the bull cites impressive TTM profit spikes [E21], the yearly operating margin trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E32], and the median return on equity over 10 years sits at a paltry 2% [E26], with a 3-year median ROE of just 7% [E28]. Conceded: [E9, E10, E30, E31] that current efficiency metrics and short-term margins look strong against sector benchmarks. However, the bull glosses over the severe structural vulnerability of a current ratio of just 1.14x, leaving an inadequate, thin buffer [E38], while total borrowings actually ticked up to Rs 350 Cr [E39]. Finally, praising sector tailwinds ignores the extreme risk embedded in the equity's profile, including an annualized volatility of 53.6% and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -91.3% [E53, E54].
